evidence.estrutura: Gillard governed through Australia’s federal parliamentary institutions and national policy frameworks; moderate national coordination within federalism.
evidence.representacao: Her parliamentary career and premiership strongly support competitive representative democracy.
evidence.poder: Her government accepted ordinary security institutions and strong border-management measures while remaining constitutional; moderate order/regulatory orientation.
evidence.imigracao: Her asylum policies, including offshore and regional processing proposals, were comparatively restrictive despite broader multicultural Australian politics.
evidence.diplomacia: She maintained close U.S. alliance ties and active regional diplomacy, making her more security-aligned than pacifist.
evidence.intervencao: Her government accepted alliance commitments and overseas defense engagement; moderate willingness to intervene rather than non-interventionism.
evidence.economia: Australian Labor under Gillard combined private markets with Fair Work labor regulation, public education and social policy; center-left mixed economy.
evidence.controle: Workplace regulation and public programs support moderate state coordination, below command planning.
evidence.comercio: Australia remained strongly committed to international trade and regional economic integration; open-trade orientation.
evidence.religiao: Gillard has publicly described herself as an atheist and governed in secular terms.
evidence.moral: Her record is mixed: strong gender/social-inclusion politics but opposition to same-sex marriage while prime minister prevents a maximal progressive score.
evidence.tecnologia: Education, infrastructure and modern public administration support pragmatic pro-technology policy.
